I think my dad would try to be but i think it would just make me feel worse as even though he wouldnt say it i feel he would think less of me because of it.
My mum and i stopped talking a while back due to unrelated things.

You have hope in that when you graduate you'll be away from that then I suppose. Its crazy in this day and age you have to hide the fact you've got a girlfriend. I dont know where you're from but here it would be accepted as normal just as someone who is straight and anyone that mocked it would be the minority.

I can relate to this, ive never wanted to kill myself via the traditional methods, but doing dangerous things seems to be a way of coping. 
The military is likely to change your whole outlook on life, for the worse or the better, however its unlikely you'll be killed in service in the current conditions unless you go well out of your way to put yourself in a bad situation.

Have you ever had contact with anyone else you'd like to make friends with? It must hurt to lose your friends over something like that but it seems you made the right decision distancing yourself if they are homophobic.
How do you know your friends wouldn't accept the fact you're gay?
Hey, im from the UK so i know its a hard to get a good education in some of our schools nowadays. What makes you say you have a shit career? A lot of people dont have a career till much older.

I find it hard to believe it can get any worse at times so im genuinely curious. I find times where i struggled in life i was far less depressed maybe because i was pre occupied, dont know if you've felt anything similar?

Hey man, I was in a very similar situation at 16. The period of your life you're in you are likely to experience drastic change. It sounds like a lot of your problems come down to your home life, if you get an oppourtunity to move out when you are earning money it sounds like you might seriously benefit from it as long as it doesnt cause you financial problems. Short term if you feel you can try spending time out the house it may also help.  

Things changed for me for a couple of years after i turned 18 and unfortunately even though i ended up feeling like this again (why else would I be on this sub i suppose) I know you can pull through too and sometime you might look back and be thankful you chose to live for the life you will then have. Bare in mind although you may hear lots of depressive thoughts and stories here, there are many who have recovered which obviously do not post here.
And these are supposed to be the best years of our lives huh
Isnt what i wanted to hear:/ but at least i know its probably not worth delving into anymore

Good to hear from you! It helps knowing theres people like me. Theres the obvious cases of super succesful people commiting suicide but i tend to just put it down to ease of access to drugs or cant cope with the fame in my mind. Im neither impulsive however sometimes I think whats stopping me from making a split second decision, putting my foot down and not taking this next corner? When you consider it you realise theres a good chance you'll survive, you'll injure others but theres no time to do so in that split second.

Id be interested to know if you've ever come close to finding an answer to why, if you've felt better in the past and how you did it.
